newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIA says currency moves affecting revenue.
newsitem.headline: SIA says currency moves affecting revenue.

text.p: The strength of the Singapore dollar and weakness of the Japanese yen are hitting Singapore Airlines Ltd (SIA)'s bottomline, SIA deputy chairman and chief executive officer Cheong Choong Kong said on Wednesday.

Cheong told Reuters in an interview that while the Singapore dollar had been relatively stable against the U.S. dollar, it had strengthened sharply against the yen and to a lesser extent against the German mark.
Japan was a major market for the national carrier, he said.
"We lost Singapore S$90 million in the first half due to the strong Singapore dollar," he said.
"The Japanese yen seems to be dropping without any bottom and that is frightening," Cheong said.
He said local yields in overseas markets were depressed due to the strong Singapore dollar as well as keen competition from other airlines.
"Local fares should improve in the second half but then (we) would still have to contend with the strength of the Singapore dollar," said Cheong.
The weakness of the yen and mark was a major factor in lower passenger yields, he said.
Overall yield fell 6.7 percent for the first half ended September 30, 1996, the company reported on Monday.
SIA reported a lower operating profit of S$468 million during the six-month period, down $60 million or 11.4 percent from the same period in 1995.
"The weakness of the yen cost us a lot because the Japanese market is a big market for us. The yen has fallen a lot against the Sing dollar," said Cheong.
He said the yen was on average some 17 percent lower against the Singapore dollar between April and September this year than it had been in the same period last year.
Japan and the United States are group's largest markets outside Singapore.
Both markets contribute about 10 to 15 percent each to SIA's group revenue, Cheong said.
He said that while the Singapore dollar looked like being flat against the U.S. in the near term, against the Japanese yen the outlook was still uncertain.
